messages:
sara_cook: FYI AcmePay flagged a sudden jump in rerank scores after last night's model push. They said identical request/response pairs now reorder. No 5xxs, just score deltas. attaching sample.

miguel: can you paste the exact request body + model name they hit? also which region/route?

sara_cook: pasted below (redacted keys). model they hit: reranker-2026-03-v1 -> we swapped tokenizer in that deploy. route: /v1/rerank. region: us-west2.

sara_cook: ```json
{
  "model": "reranker-2026-03-v1",
  "inputs": [
    {"query": "refund for duplicate charge", "candidates": ["refund charge duplicated", "how to dispute charge", "refund policy"]},
    {"query": "invoice not matching total", "candidates": ["invoice total mismatch", "why my invoice different", "billing discrepancy"]}
  ]
}
```

miguel: got it. what are the scores they see vs what we returned historically?

sara_cook: they ran the same payload against our snapshot of yesterday (reranker-2026-02) and got top candidate index 0 for both queries. With the new model, top candidate flipped to index 1 on first query and scores changed by ~0.12. They attached full score arrays.

sara_cook: ```
// yesterday (reranker-2026-02): [0.78, 0.67, 0.45]
// today (reranker-2026-03-v1): [0.66, 0.78, 0.40]
```

alex.k: quick hypothesis: we shipped tokenizer mapping change in v1 — padding token id moved from 0 -> 1 for new tokenizer. If batching/prefix padding is applied differently the model could see shifted positions (off-by-one) which affects attention masks.

jess_ops: @alex.k that would explain it if the client payload included trailing spaces or explicit pad tokens. Do we have logs showing token ids pre/post?

miguel: I can repro locally if I run tokenizer v2026-03 on their input. Will do a token diff.

deploy-bot: Deployment completed: reranker-2026-03-v1 -> us-west2 (deploy id: d-8901). Change: tokenizer update, attention fix, batching opt.

eng-ml-lead: tagging for ML: this smells like tokenization/pad boundary behavior. Also check KV cache alignment when using continuous batching — could be an indexing mismatch.

miguel: local token diff:
```
// input: "refund for duplicate charge"
// tokens v2026-02: [101, 345, 72, 889, 204]
// tokens v2026-03: [101, 345, 72, 889, 204, 0]  // extra pad token appended
```

miguel: v2026-03 adds trailing pad in our tokenizer when input ends with punctuation? not sure. Seems the model receives different seq_len which shifts positional embeddings.

alex.k: if positional ids are shifted relative to attention mask we can easily flip relative comparisons used in reranker head. Need to confirm whether pos ids or attention mask computation changed in serving runtime for new tokenizer.

jess_ops: action items: 1) Acquire 10 reproducible examples from customer (sara) 2) Run end-to-end compare on both model snapshots including token ids, attention masks, and raw logits 3) Open a block ticket to pause rollout in other regions until root cause identified 4) Notify customer with ETA.

sara_cook: I asked AcmePay to provide 10 examples and we'll attach logs. They've already been pretty sensitive about rank flips so we promised daily updates.

eng-ml-lead: I'll take 2). If logs show pad-id insertion, we should either 1) revert tokenizer mapping or 2) add a normalization preprocessor on the serving path to strip trailing pads for rerank requests. But first confirm whether this change was intentional upstream.

miguel: reproducing full E2E now. small note: when I re-run the same request but force disable batching (single-request path) the scores match the old model. When batching is on, we see the flip. That points strongly at batching alignment + pad handling.

alex.k: nice catch. that indicates runtime batching logic probably didn't respect new tokenizer's pad_id. It may be applying pad_id from config (old default=0). We changed tokenizer pad_id to 2 in the model artifact but runtime metadata remained 0 for this deploy.

eng-ml-lead: estimate: high priority patch to runtime to read pad_id from model metadata + small canary in us-west2. If patch takes >4h, consider rolling back reranker-2026-03-v1 in us-west2 to reranker-2026-02.

sara_cook: customer asked for a rollback option ASAP. I'll coordinate with CS to offer temporary mitigation (pin to older model) while you fix.

jess_ops: filing incident INC-345. Recording repro steps and linking commit diff for tokenizer.

miguel: attaching quick repro command for eng to run:
```bash
# compare responses against two snapshots
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '@payload.json' | jq .scores > scores_new.txt
# run against snapshot
REDWOOD_MODEL=snapshots/reranker-2026-02 \
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d @payload.json | jq .scores > scores_old.txt
# compare
diff scores_old.txt scores_new.txt
```

alex.k: I'm starting a runtime patch branch now (runtime: respect model.tokenizer.pad_id for batch padding). Will add unit test that simulates mixed pad_id inputs.

sara_cook: thanks. I'll keep AcmePay updated. tagging @jess_ops for communication. :thumbsup:

eng-ml-lead: once we have logs and a patched runtime build, let's run a small canary with the customer examples and confirm stability. If stable, roll forward; otherwise rollback.

sara_cook: noted. last: please capture exact token diffs/snapshots to include in customer postmortem.

miguel: will upload artifacts to the incident folder shortly.

jess_ops: copying internal SLA note to the incident doc and pinging sales for any potential credit requests.

sara_cook: closing loop for now — will update once we have a repro set and eng patch.
